title: Far person
purpose: Small-in-frame recall collapse and boundary chatter. Re-fly this whenever preprocess.c changes: the Sep 11 resize study showed nearest-neighbour downscaling costs recall specifically on small people.

subjects.name: subj_person_target
subjects.note: Measured in THIS scene, camera inside the room: 0.905 at 6.5 m. The far wall is at x = 7, so 6.5 m is the practical maximum range available.

prediction.rationale: CORRECTION to spec_scenes.md section 3. The spec set this scene at 6.5 m because P1 supposedly collapsed 0.998 -> 0.588 between 4.5 and 6.0 m. That falloff is an ARTIFACT: build_person_scene.py --preview places the camera at person_x - dist, and with the default person_x = 2.5 the 6.0/8.0/10.0 m probes sat at x = -3.5/-5.5/-7.5, i.e. OUTSIDE the room, behind the back wall at x = -3. probe/person_far/preview_d6.0.png is a blank white frame, so 0.588 is the model's reading of a featureless wall, not of a distant person. Rendered properly from inside this room, a 1.70 m person at 6.5 m reads 0.905 and should be followed. This room cannot place a person in the boundary band by range alone; a genuine small-in-frame test needs a longer room or a shorter subject.

limitations: Does NOT exercise the [0.45, 0.70) boundary band, contrary to the spec's intent: 6.5 m is the longest sight line this room allows and a person is still detected at 0.905 there. It remains the right flight-level regression detector for preprocess.c changes (smallest in-frame person available), but it is not the near-threshold scene. s10 is.
